verdict.rationale: Entrust documents OAuth client-credentials authentication that issues short-lived access tokens, and says this method gives 'more granular control over the scope of access'. That is first-party support for scoped, least-privilege API credentials. The evidence does not show what scopes exist, how they are assigned, or any per-agent credential management, so the depth is unproven. Missing for 10: a documented list of scopes and permissions, a way to issue and revoke separate credentials per agent or client, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: This authentication method gives you more granular control over the scope of access.
Entrust recommends generating short-lived OAuth access tokens for API authentication using client credentials grant.
The Entrust Identity Verification API uses OAuth access and token-based authentication for both its sandbox and live environments.
